ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Financial Transaction Reports Act, FTRA), Act No. 17205, as amended; Enforcement Decree of the FTRA; Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee Act, Act No. 17683, as amended; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 17450, as amended; Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) AML/CFT Guidelines; Financial Services Commission Regulations on Beneficial Ownership Identification and Customer Due Diligence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea, District Court Registration Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Public document. For Hague Apostille Convention states: issue certified copy from Korean registry, then submit directly to the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille Section. For non-Hague states: submit the registry certificate to the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs Consular Legalization Division, then present it to the embassy or consulate of the destination state in Seoul. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel, mutually exclusive routes and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Business Registration Certificate / Tax Clearance Status)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service, District Tax Office in the jurisdiction of the registered address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Public document. For Hague states: obtain a certified business registration certificate from the National Tax Service and have the certificate apostilled by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For non-Hague states: obtain Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular legalization and then authentication by the destination country consulate in Seoul. Do not combine apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney Appointing Incorporation Agent and Bank Mandate Holder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chusik Hoesa (confirmed by its incorporators or initial shareholders) and a Korean Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private document. Execute in writing, notarize signatures before a Korean notary, then for Hague states obtain a Ministry of Foreign Affairs apostille. For non-Hague states, after notarization, obtain Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular legalization and then the destination state consulate legalization in Seoul. The apostille route and consular legalization route are alternative and must not be applied sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Certified or Notarized Version)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Notary Public or the Supreme Court Registry Office that received the articles
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Public or notarized instrument. For Hague states: notarized copy plus Ministry of Foreign Affairs apostille. For non-Hague states: notarized copy, then Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular legalization, then destination state consulate legalization in Seoul. Use either apostille or consular legalization according to the destination state; never chain both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (including UBO certificate validations and transaction account status)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank where the initial capital account or settlement account will be maintained
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private document. The bank's authorized officer signature must first be notarized before a Korean notary. For Hague states, apply to the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for an apostille. For non-Hague states, apply for Ministry of Foreign Affairs consular legalization followed by destination state consulate legalization in Seoul. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives and shall not be sequentially chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All legal shareholders, controlling persons, 25%-or-greater ultimate beneficial owners, directors, representatives, and authorized signatories must be screened before filing and rescreened periodically against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit AML/CFT framework, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the United States OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists, the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act sanctions designations, Korean domestic consolidated watchlists, PEP databases maintained by criminal justice and tax authorities, adverse media, insolvency, regulatory enforcement, and disqualification registers. Any active or former senior public official, close associate, or family member triggering PEP status requires enhanced due diligence including source of wealth and source of funds evidence, approval by the AML compliance officer, and real-time transaction filtering before and after incorporation. All findings must be documented in a written UBO and sanctions screening memorandum and retained for at least five years under KoFIU standards.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (I-REG / IRRO Online Company Registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be written in the Korean alphabet in the official registry. For a Chusik Hoesa the suffix indicating stock corporation status must appear in Korean transliteration as Chusik Hoesa at the end of the name. Foreign English words may be used only in Korean transliteration on the official registration, and an English-only trade name cannot replace the Korean registered name. Four-tier naming conventions apply: first, a distinctive expanded business identifier; second, a business-object description consistent with ISIC 4791 electronic B2B wholesale platform activity; third, the suffix Chusik Hoesa; and fourth, no prohibited administrative or geographic element. Where a foreign parent name is transliterated, the applicant must submit a transliteration table and obtain registry examiner approval.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Korean registry rejects the proposed name, counsel must obtain a written rejection reason from the registry examiner and prepare a corrected electronic filing within fourteen days, substituting the distinctive first tier while preserving the business-object description and Chusik Hoesa suffix. If the registry again refuses, the applicant may file an immediate appeal to the competent regional District Court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act within two weeks from the rejection notice, attaching the name-search result, the intended business scope, and the transliteration and trademark clearance evidence. Alternatively, the applicant may reserve a new name through the I-REG portal and restart the clearance process; no administrative appeal to the tax authority is available because name clearance is a judicial registry function.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox used as the sole registered address is generally rejected by the Korean National Tax Service and commercial banks for a B2B cross-border platform. The registry requires a real, exclusive or supported physical address in Korea, and banks opening Swift wire and Alibaba Pay settlement accounts apply a substance test requiring lease agreements, utility bills, signage, and employee or agent presence at the address. A virtual office may be tolerated only as an additional correspondence address, never as the principal place of business for corporate registration, tax invoicing, or AML KYC purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-to-high quantified risk of an unannounced municipal tax or registry inspection within the first twelve months, estimated at 35 percent, increasing above 60 percent within three years for an e-commerce marketplace. Checklist: verify that a visible external sign shows the exact registered Chusik Hoesa name; lease contract matches the registry address; physical desks, computing equipment, telecommunications, and data servers or clearly contracted cloud infrastructure are present; tax invoices and bank records carry the same registered address; employees or authorized staff can answer on-site questions; and a local VAT and transaction ledger is produced on demand. Failure to maintain this commercial substance can trigger de-registration, bank account suspension, and penalties.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary fee schedule under the Notary Public Act, ranging KRW 20,000 to KRW 100,000 (USD 15 to USD 80) depending on document length.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory apostille fee of approximately KRW 3,000 (USD 2.50) per document; estimated USD 25 for a five-document bundle.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Consular legalization protocol fee for non-Hague destination states only, if applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea and the embassy or consulate of the destination state in Seoul
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee schedules vary; estimated USD 50 per document for destination consulate legalization plus MOFA processing fee of approximately USD 10.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation registration tax and court registration surcharge for a Chusik Hoesa with no statutory minimum capital

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000 of 1962 (as consolidated), Articles 289 (Articles of Incorporation), 290 (Articles Clauses), 292 (Validity of the Articles), 295 (Subscription Initial Shares), 300 (Payment of Subscriptions and Formalities), 317 (Registration of Incorporation), 318 (Effective Time of Incorporation), 329 (Share Capital), 383 (Board of Directors), 393 (Authority of the Board), 409 (Statutory Auditor), 416 (New Shares), 461 (Minimum Capital) and the Local Tax Act, Presidential Decree No. 22395.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Section, Civil Affairs Division, Local District Court with jurisdiction over the company's registered office (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Commercial Registry); filings may be submitted electronically through the Korean Court E-filing System (IROS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Registration Application and supporting Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan), filed under Article 317 of the Korean Commercial Act, together with the capital payment certificate, directors' consent forms and initial board minutes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Chusik Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act; a company may be incorporated with nominal capital. However, market practice for a B2B cross-border platform requires at least KRW 10,000,000 (approximately USD 7,500) of paid-in capital to satisfy bank misconduct due diligence and payment service onboarding. The full subscription amount must be deposited into a temporary bank subscription account in the Republic of Korea before incorporation registration, and the bank must issue a certificate of payment for the shares. No blocked escrow account is mandated by the Commercial Act. If the marketplace will hold customer or merchant settlement funds, a trust or escrow arrangement may be triggered under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and the FSC regulatory guidance.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Commercial Registry (for company name conflict checking) and a duly commissioned Notary Public in the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoters shall obtain a certified abstract of the proposed company name from the Commercial Registry IROS online system or by visiting the court registry. The Articles must state the corporate name, principal objects, registered office address, total authorized share capital, number and par value of shares, method of forming the corporation, and the names of the directors and auditor. All promoters must sign or, where represented, execute a power of attorney; signatures on the Articles must be notarized by a notary public to certify identity and authenticity. If the name is identical or deceptively similar to an existing company, a new name must be adopted. The notarial certificate should be obtained in multiple counterpart copies for subsequent step use.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identification card of each promoter
Proposed Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Name availability confirmation from IROS Commercial Registry
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or letter of intent)
Power of attorney if promoter appears by proxy
Corporate constitutional information schedule for B2B marketplace objects
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry objects on grounds of confusing similarity or statutory clause omission, the promoters must amend the Articles and re-notarize the revised version. Any correction notice issued by the court can be cured by filing supplementary documents within the prescribed period, preserving priority over other applicants.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Bank Certificate of Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed commercial bank in the Republic of Korea (e.g., Shinhan, Kookmin, Woori, Hana, or KEB Hana Bank) through the corporate services desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the notarized Articles are obtained, the promoters shall open a temporary share subscription deposit account in the name of the company being formed or one promoter, depending on bank policy, with a Korean commercial bank. Each subscriber must transfer the agreed subscription amount into that account. The bank will verify the identity of the subscribers under anti-money laundering rules and issue a certificate of deposit of paid-in capital, indicating the amount, account number, and date. This certificate must be presented to the court as evidence that all initial shares are fully paid in. Funds should remain in the account until the incorporation registration is accepted, after which they may be transferred to the company's main operating account once the corporate bank mandate is established.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Passport and alien registration card or Korean ID of each subscriber
Corporate account opening application form
Source of funds evidence for AML compliance
Power of attorney if submitting through a corporate formation agent
Initial board resolution authorizing the bank and capital deposit (if already adopted)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank suspends the account opening on AML or CDD concerns, the promoters must provide additional beneficial ownership declarations, source of funds evidence, or corporate transaction explanations. If the bank remains unsatisfied, another commercial bank may be used without restarting the incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration at the Local District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the company's registered office, or online via the IROS certified e-filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporation registration application must be filed within two weeks from the date of capital payment if all shares are paid in cash. The applicant must submit the notarized Articles, the certificate of share payment, the incorporation meeting report, the first board resolution, written consent for each director and statutory auditor, and an appointment report. The court assesses the statutory requirements, calculates registration tax under the Local Tax Act and court fees, and verifies the company name. Upon approval, the court assigns a corporate registration number and issues a certified corporate register (deung-gi-bon) and a certificate of corporate seal. The corporate existence commences on the effective registration date, not before.
required_dossiers: Application for commercial registration (court form)
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank certificate of paid-in capital
Minutes of the incorporation meeting and first board meeting
Consent forms of directors and statutory auditor
Power of attorney for filing agent, if any
Certificate of registered office lease or usage permission
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration officer issues a correction notice, the applicant must supply the missing documentation or rectify invalid clauses within the stated deadline. Failure to cure will result in dismissal, but refiling is allowed once the defect is corrected. An adverse final order may be appealed by filing an objection with the court of registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office of the National Tax Service (NTS) for the company's tax residence district; online via the HomeTax system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court registration is complete, the company must file a business registration application with the district tax office within 20 days of business commencement, using HomeTax. The application should specify the industry code corresponding to online wholesale and retail platform operations and declare the corporate value added tax and electronic tax invoice obligations. The tax office will issue a corporate business registration certificate with a unique tax registration number. This certificate is necessary for issuing tax invoices, opening bank accounts in the corporate name, importing goods, signing contracts, and enabling cross-border payment rails. The company must also file corporate income tax, VAT returns, and withholding obligations for salaries.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of commercial registration (deung-gi-bon)
Corporate seal certificate and specimen seal
Business registration application form (HomeTax)
Lease contract or proof of business address
Identification documents of officers and beneficial owners
Company officers' appointment report or board resolution certifying management
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the address or business purpose, present the lease agreement, floor plan, or a revised purpose statement. If the application is rejected, correct the form and resubmit through HomeTax or at the civil tax service window; a prompt cure avoids penalties for operating without business registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation E-Commerce Platform Report and Final Governance Implementation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (for the communications sale business report under the Electronic Commerce Act), the Korea Fair Trade Commission (for platform terms compliance) and the company's principal bank for final account activation and payment rail setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: As the entity will operate an electronic B2B wholesale marketplace, the Representative Director must file a communications sale business report with the competent tax office, indicating the platform's operator identity and URL. The company must also register payment gateway and settlement infrastructure under its own legal name, execute the corporate account mandate for SWIFT wire and Alibaba Pay, complete the corporate seal registration, and adopt standard terms and conditions for platform users under KFTC e-commerce guidelines. If the business scales to handle consumer transactions or additional cross-border payment data, a privacy impact assessment and Information Security Management System certification may be required, but this is not an industrial license.
required_dossiers: Business registration certificate from the NTS
Corporate seal and certificate
Domain registration certificate and server or hosting contract, if applicable
Model platform terms and privacy policy
Board resolution approving banking mandate and payment rails
Communications sale business report application (if subject to the report)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the communications sale business report is returned for insufficiency, renew the application with corrected business description and platform information. If payment service providers require additional bank branch KYC, provide the beneficial ownership registry and board banking resolution. For KFTC guidance, remedy any unfair terms within the corrective order period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable – the entity is a digital B2B marketplace platform under ISIC 4791 and operates no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facility. The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) and the Korea Industrial Complex Corporation have no operating license remit over this pure electronic intermediary.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable – no industrial operating license is required. However, the company will file a communications sale business report with the National Tax Service and comply with the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce and the Korea Fair Trade Commission platform guidelines.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable – Ministry of Environment and Korea Environmental Industry & Technology Institute (KEITI) do not require an EIA for a pure online B2B platform with no physical footprint.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no EIA, no environmental registration, and no preliminary environmental review because there is no physical construction, equipment installation, or emission source.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable – zero wastewater discharge, zero stationary VOC emissions, and no hazardous waste handling. Server hosting and data centers are operated by third-party cloud providers, who bear their own environmental obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable – no fire safety certificate, structural load inspection, or civil defense fire permit is required for a non-industrial digital office environment. For the ordinary office lease, the employer must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act and maintain basic fire prevention measures under the Fire Prevention and Safety Control Act; no factory building permits or operational physical clearances apply.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online registration and filing portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity (including a B2B marketplace operator) that commences a business or establishes a fixed place of business in Korea must apply for a Business Registration Certificate at the competent district NTS office, or electronically through HomeTax, within 20 days of commencement of business. Required submissions include the foreign entity's certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, evidence of a Korean fixed place of business, an appointed Korean tax representative's power of attorney and identification, a board resolution appointing the representative, and, where available, an apostilled or certified company extraction from the home registry. The filing generates a 10-digit Korean Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN), which simultaneously serves as the VAT registration number. No separate VAT registration is required beyond this business registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not provide a check-the-box or similar elective entity classification regime. A Chusik Hoesa (Stock Corporation) is automatically subjected to entity-level taxation under the Korean Corporate Tax Act. No hybrid mismatch election is available to the taxpayer.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No economic turnover threshold for corporate entities. Any corporation engaged in business in Korea, regardless of turnover, must complete business registration and VAT registration within 20 days of business commencement. Simplified taxpayer thresholds (KRW 80 million for wholesale/retail/manufacturing and KRW 30 million for service businesses) apply only to individual proprietors, not to a Chusik Hoesa.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korean VAT law requires every registered business operator supplying goods or services to issue a tax invoice. For general taxpayers, the tax invoice must be issued as an electronic tax invoice transmitted to the NTS through the HomeTax electronic tax invoice platform (e-Scro) no later than the day after the supply date. The NTS assigns and validates electronic signatures and unique invoice numbers; no physical fiscal stamp is required. Although Korea does not operate a full real-time fiscal clearance system comparable to Latin American models, the e-tax invoice transmission constitutes immediate near-real-time tax administration control and supports anti-fraud digital stamping.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating applies where goods are sold to a nonresident purchaser, the goods are physically exported outside Korea, and the export is evidenced by an export declaration accepted by Korea Customs Service. Qualifying offshore digital services supplied to nonresident business customers are zero-rated when the service is consumed or used outside Korea and is declared on the VAT return with supporting service contracts and foreign exchange receipt proof. For a B2B cross-border marketplace operator, each underlying transaction must satisfy the legal export definition and be documented per Korean VAT and Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration (UNI-PASS entry)
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill for airfreight)
Banking proof of offshore payment: Foreign Exchange Transaction Confirmation (Overseas Remittance Receipt Confirmation) issued by a licensed foreign exchange bank in Korea in the exporter's name
Evidence of the underlying B2B order or contract between the Korean supplier and the nonresident purchaser
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the export documentation is missing, incomplete, or the foreign exchange proceeds are not repatriated through recognized Korean banking channels within 180 calendar days from the export declaration date, the NTS may revoke zero-rating, assess 10% VAT on the transaction value, and impose overdue interest. Under the VAT Act, failure to report or underreporting can attract additional tax penalties of up to 20% for negligent errors and 40% for fraudulent or hidden transactions. The statute of limitations on NTS collection is five years from the relevant tax payment date; this extends to ten years in cases of intentional tax evasion or false accounting. Gross misrepresentation may also trigger criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea, acting as the central bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance as the foreign exchange policy authority
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberal but tightly supervised foreign exchange regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA), collectively administered by the Bank of Korea, the Ministry of Economy and Finance, and authorized foreign exchange banks. Current-account transactions, including cross-border B2B marketplace payments, service fees, royalties, and ordinary operating settlements, are freely convertible upon submission of a transaction confirmation to the designated bank; prior approval is not required. Capital-account transactions, including foreign direct investment into a Chusik Hoesa, inbound loans, and equity contributions, are subject to a report/declaration framework, with the FDI report filed through a foreign exchange bank before funds are remitted and a foreign investment registration certificate issued. Profit remittance is permitted offshore via a bank after corporate income tax is paid and the board declares a dividend subject to a 20 or 22 percent withholding tax plus local surtax, with treaty relief available where applicable. Actual treasury hurdles include documentary evidence of audited retained earnings, tax payment certificates, bank confirmation of the underlying FDI report, and strict matching between the remittance purpose code and the underlying transaction. KRW is not freely usable overseas and must be converted via onshore banks, but no mandatory surrender of export earnings is imposed. On balance, convertibility is robust for genuine trade and investment flows, with the primary friction being documentation and beneficial ownership verification rather than convertibility denial.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under FETA and the Foreign Trade Act, export proceeds received for goods or digital B2B services must be collected through a Korean foreign exchange bank within six months from the export invoice date or service completion date unless an extension is approved by the Korea Customs Service or the Bank of Korea. There is no mandatory conversion ratio in the current regime; exporters may retain these receipts in foreign-currency deposit accounts, convert them to KRW at market rates, or use them for eligible payments. However, the bank must receive proof of the underlying export transaction and the exporter unique identification number, and the proceeds must flow through a payment rail that enables reconciliation with Korea Customs Service trade statistics. Overdue and unreported export proceeds are reportable as foreign exchange violations and may attract penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Foreign Investment Capital Deposit Account)
Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and multi-currency)
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Foreign fintech EMIs are legally barred from issuing domestic Korean corporate IBANs or opening local KRW settlement accounts under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. They are also not authorized to act as a designated foreign exchange bank for receiving export proceeds. Their viable role is limited to downstream collection or payment aggregation for marketplace buyers, with funds ultimately routed through a licensed Korean bank. Treasury must therefore treat SWIFT MT103 through a domestic tier-1 bank as the only compliant primary clearing rail. Overall feasibility rating: LOW for primary corporate banking; MEDIUM only as an ancillary payment interface if the EMI partners with a licensed Korean bank, and that bank remains the depository institution of record.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Korean-incorporated Chusik Hoesa, at least one signing officer must appear in person at the branch for corporate seal registration and basic operational account opening, unless the bank permits a power-of-attorney holder such as a local corporate secretary or certified accountant to attend. For foreign-based representative officers, the bank normally requires a remote video interview conducted through a Korean consulate or an apostilled durable power of attorney executed before a Korean notary public. Full remote onboarding without any in-person or consular identity validation is not accepted for capital escrow accounts. The bank also mandates presentation of the original or certified copy of the business registration certificate, corporate registry excerpts, shareholder resolution for account opening, and the corporate seal impression certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner discontinuity when the Chusik Hoesa holds a shareholder chain through Hong Kong or Singapore intermediate vehicles, and the Korean bank cannot readily identify the natural-person controller under FATF Recommendation 24 standards.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certified legalization of the shareholder registry, all constitutive documents of each intermediate entity, a complete ownership chart signed by each intermediate director, proof of address and passport copies for each natural-person UBO, a beneficial owner statement in the bank-prescribed format, and a Hong Kong or Singapore company search extract showing the entire equity ladder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection sourced from a jurisdiction with weak AML enforcement or routed through a virtual-asset exchange gateway, creating a source-of-wealth red flag during underwriting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble twelve months of upstream account statements showing the full remittance trail without layering, board resolution authorizing the capital call, executed share subscription agreement for each non-resident shareholder, tax residence certificate for each transferring entity, a detailed wealth breakdown if injected funds appear disproportionate to declared income, and a legal opinion from foreign counsel confirming that the source of funds is compliant with both the home-country law and Korean FETA.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure or adverse media connected to marketplace merchants, particularly because digital B2B platforms may not pre-screen indirect beneficiaries of remittances.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a transaction-level sanctions screening report for each counterparty and final beneficiary, a compliance officer attestation that the platform applies real-time OFAC/EU/UN denial screening and IP-blocking for sanctioned geographies, contractual terms that prohibit sanctioned parties from using the marketplace, and a notarized declaration appending the applicable export-control classification or digital goods license for each high-value order.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering indicators from platform sales including mismatched pricing, volume anomalies, or back-to-back settlement to third-party accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the bank with an accounting-system export containing unique order IDs, digital delivery proof, escrow payout reports from the marketplace operator, merchant billing and invoice copies, the company published price list or quotation methodology for B2B goods, and a reconciliation packet matching each received export payment to the corresponding order, including Korean tax e-invoice files and customs declarations for any physical shipments.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route FDI capital through a designated foreign exchange bank in Korea. First file the foreign direct investment notification with the bank or Invest Korea under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and obtain a registration certificate. Then open a Foreign Investment Capital Deposit Account in KRW or foreign currency with the same bank. Arrange the inbound remittance as an SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident investor, using the applicable Bank of Korea foreign exchange purpose code for direct investment equity contribution and clearly identifying the beneficiary Korean bank and the Foreign Investment Capital Deposit Account number. After the funds are credited, the bank verifies the inward remittance and automatically reports it to the Bank of Korea. Capital may be deployed into the operational account only after the foreign investment registration certificate indicates completed capital verification. Any future dividend repatriation or capital return must be executed through the same registered bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for low-value, repetitive B2B digital marketplace settlements, with full invoice references and clear beneficiary and payment purpose details appended to the cover message. For wholesale physical goods, use Commercial Letters of Credit, particularly irrevocable and confirmed credits issued by a Korean bank and advised through a cross-border correspondent. For established trade partners with acceptable sovereign risk, use Documentary Collections, whether documents against payment or documents against acceptance, supported by a fixed bill of lading or electronic delivery proof. Every outbound payment requires underlying trade documentation retained for at least five years and a prohibition on payments to any sanctioned jurisdiction. All FX conversions for disbursement must be handled by the licensed bank to maintain FX reporting and regulatory purpose code integrity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward foreign exchange contracts offered by licensed Korean banks, limited to the notional volume of underlying export receivables or import payables and maturing within the standard FETA trade-payment horizon.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) approved by the Bank of Korea for hedging non-trade capital-account exposures, with settlement in KRW or a permitted foreign currency and no speculative unlawful leverage.

Cross-currency swaps (KRW/USD) or FX option collars, only where the underlying exposure is a registered FDI capital balance or a genuine operational current-account flow, and where the bank has issued a product suitability confirmation with prescribed maturity and exposure matching.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Tax Return with Approved Financial Statements Annexed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end; for an off-cycle fiscal year, within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; a one-month extension to April 30 is allowed when the return is prepared and signed by a licensed tax accountant.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled return attracts an additional tax equal to 20% of the computed deficiency (10% for general under-declaration), plus late-payment interest at 0.025% per day (approximately 9.125% per annum, adjusted quarterly under the Framework Act on National Taxes). Persistent non-compliance triggers asset seizure, tax collection compulsory execution, business identity freeze, and after repeated public notices may contribute to administrative strike-off of the corporate registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Local Corporate Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: The competent Si/Gun/Gu local government tax office of the registered head office in South Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the national corporate tax return: generally March 31, or April 30 when the tax accountant-prepared extension applies; non-December fiscal years follow the 3-month post-year-end rule.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or underpayment triggers a local tax additional charge of 20%-30% of the deficiency, daily late-payment interest at 0.025%, local tax lien registration on business assets, and refusal to issue the tax clearance certificate needed for certain regulatory renewals and banking relationships.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Meeting and Approval of Separate Annual Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of record; finalised statements and meeting minutes must be maintained at the registered head office and, where applicable, submitted to the Commercial Registration Division of the competent District Court and the National Tax Service with the annual return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the close of the business year; the meeting must be convened inside this window and may be extended only with court approval for exceptional circumstances.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be subject to an administrative fine of not more than KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 3,800) for failure to call the meeting without just cause; a shareholder may obtain a court order requiring the meeting to be convened; repeated failure can expose the company to judicial dissolution proceedings and blockage of lawful dividend distributions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report (where the external audit threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: For listed and public-interest companies, the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through its DART electronic disclosure system; for non-listed audited Chusik Hoesa, the final audit report is submitted to shareholders at the Annual Shareholders' Meeting and attached to the corporate tax return filed with the National Tax Service.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The audit must be completed in time for presentation at the Annual Shareholders' Meeting, which must be held within 3 months of the fiscal year-end; the report is normally finalised with the annual financial statements and included in the corporate tax filing by March 31 or April 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or to submit the audit report may lead to administrative fines of up to KRW 50,000,000 (approximately USD 38,000), designation of an auditor by the Securities and Futures Commission at the company's cost, publication of non-compliance, and invalidation of tax-beneficial treatment where an audited report is a statutory precondition.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Register and Registered Office/Agent Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: The business registration desk of the local district tax office (NTS) responsible for the business place, with supporting records retained by the corporate secretarial agent for court or tax inspection.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by January 31 unless a business-site closure or address relocation occurs; any change to the registered office, representative director, statutory auditor, or line of business must be registered with the Commercial Registration Division within the statutory change-notification window and with NTS within 30 days after the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report a change is subject to an additional penalty under the Framework Act on National Taxes and, for registry matters, to an administrative fine of up to KRW 5,000,000; prolonged failure to ascertain an active registered seat can support a court-initiated administrative strike-off for a dormant corporation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Chusik Hoesa is compulsorily audited by an independent certified public accountant if any of the following applies: (a) it is a KOSPI, KOSDAQ, or KONEX listed stock company regardless of size; (b) it is a non-listed stock company whose total assets at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year are KRW 10,000,000,000 (approximately USD 7,700,000) or more; (c) it falls under the Presidential Decree composite scale criteria based on annual gross revenue (e.g. approximately KRW 50,000,000,000 or more of annual turnover) and workforce size (e.g. 100 or more full-time employees); (d) it is classified as a public-interest company under the External Audit Act, such as a financial company, insurance company, or an entity with assets of approximately KRW 2,000,000,000,000 or more; or (e) it is designated by the Financial Supervisory Service for audit because of public-interest relevance or shareholder/creditor protection needs. Even when an independent audit is not mandatory, the entity must still prepare financial statements, have them examined by directors, and obtain the approval of the Annual Shareholders' Meeting.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are mandatory for listed and public-interest companies; non-public Chusik Hoesa may apply the Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles for Small and Medium Business Entities (SME K-GAAP or simplified accounting standards) unless they voluntarily adopt K-IFRS. All statutory audits are performed under the Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA), which converge with the International Standards on Auditing.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not impose a general public UBO annual report for a private stock corporation, but the resident corporate secretarial function must confirm the shareholder register before each Annual Shareholders' Meeting and maintain the shareholder ledger at the registered head office in Korea. Any transfer of registered shares must be entered in the shareholder register without delay so that the transferee is recognised as a shareholder. For cross-border equity movements, the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act imposes a 30-day reporting window through a designated foreign exchange bank and to the National Tax Service where a non-resident acquires or transfers Korean equity interests, and the company must supply a certificate of beneficial ownership to the tax authority when treaty benefits or foreign-investor incentives are claimed. Financial institutions under the Real-Name Financial Transaction Act may independently require annual re-confirmation of the natural-person controlling beneficial owners for AML/KYC purposes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Board of Directors' Meetings
Registered Accounting Books and Supporting Vouchers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - USD 2,500 per annum for registered office address, corporate secretarial support, and registered agent services in South Korea
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 28,000 per annum for a certified independent audit of a mid-tier cross-border B2B marketplace operating as a Chusik Hoesa, depending on asset size, turnover, consolidation scope, and audit complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national Corporate Income Tax on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion, plus a 10% local income surtax, for an all-in top combined rate of 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The effective rate may be reduced under the Special Tax Reduction and Incentives Act: 100% corporate tax exemption for 5 years and 50% reduction for 2 years for eligible foreign-invested high-technology activities in Free Economic Zones; R&D tax credits; technology income transfer reductions for qualifying patented technology royalties; and venture-company investment credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Primary form: Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Calculation Statement filed electronically through HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year; a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa must file by 31 March. A short extension of up to one month is generally available only through an appointed tax representative, but the tax payment deadline is not automatically extended.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, business registration number, head office address and foreign-invested company status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean domestic place of business address of the Chusik Hoesa and, if ownership is non-resident, attach the foreign investor registration details plus the Korean tax representative particulars. Failure to name a domestic representative may render the return incomplete and trigger declarant penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Fiscal Year and Reporting Period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable year start and end dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the same twelve-month accounting cycle fixed in the Articles of Incorporation. The first return covers the period from incorporation to the fiscal year-end and cannot exceed one statutory accounting period, subject to valid short-year close.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Gross Revenue and Other Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales, B2B marketplace commission fees, subscription service income, advertising fees and other operating revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue attributable to a Mainland Korean PE under the domestic source and PE attribution rules. Cross-border platform fees earned through payment rails such as Alibaba Pay and SWIFT must be included in gross revenue to the extent the income is functionally connected to Korean economic activities or effective management.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales, wages, rent, platform processing costs, intercompany royalties and financing expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Costs payable to non-residents are deductible only if withholding tax was withheld and remitted or an applicable treaty exemption/relief was timely substantiated. Add back non-arm's-length charges; disallow payments for which no transfer pricing documentation is preserved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after statutory adjustments, loss carryforwards, tax-exempt reserves and special deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Carryforward losses are capped at the five-year statutory window and must be reconciled with a supporting schedule. Dividend distributions to shareholders are not deductible for a Chusik Hoesa, and excessive debt-to-equity finance from non-resident shareholders is recharacterized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Corporate Tax Computed and Offsets
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Progressive CIT calculation, local income surtax, foreign tax credit and prior year tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the current Korean progressive scale: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; and 24% above KRW 300 billion, plus 10% local income surtax. Foreign tax credits are claimed only on income already subject to Korean corporate tax, and treaty withholding on outbound dividends does not reduce the corporation's domestic tax on PE-derived profit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an additional tax of 10% of the unpaid corporate tax, rising to 20% after six months under the Basic Act for National Taxes. Underdeclared tax attracts a 10% additional tax, while fraudulent concealment or false returns attract a 20% penalty. Unpaid tax accrues statutory daily late-payment interest, and material false declarations constitute criminal tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying imprisonment or fines to three times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% outbound dividend withholding tax, comprising 20% national corporate income tax withholding plus 2% local income surtax, before application of any Double Tax Agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner must deliver a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the residence jurisdiction, complete the Korean Application for Reduction or Exemption of Non-Resident Withholding Tax under the Tax Convention, and submit a beneficial ownership declaration confirming the recipient is not a conduit or nominee. The application must be filed with the payer before distribution; where over-withheld, a refund application must be filed within the applicable five-year statutory limitation. Korea applies BEPS MLI and limitation-on-benefits safeguards, so the claiming entity must demonstrate substantive CIGA and no treaty shopping.

stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding is 22% for both outbound interest and royalties before treaty reduction. Treaty rates commonly reduce interest to 10% for financial institutions and 15% in other cases, and royalties to 10-15% depending on the counterparty DTA and royalty character; excessive related-party interest is additionally exposed to thin capitalization recharacterization.
